rationale: oopack_v1p8 is a small C++ benchmark dominated by tight, hot numeric loops (matrix multiplication, complex arithmetic, iterator traversal) and object-oriented dispatch, with an empty static profile so the table must be conservative. SUB and IBR get high SecurityGain/DiversityGain weights because they cheaply obscure arithmetic and control-flow edges with minimal impact on loop-heavy code; ICALL is weighted highest on SecurityGain since C++-heavy code benefits greatly from virtualizing call targets, and its modest cost is tolerable; FLA and BCF receive moderate weights because flattening and bogus control flow carry real runtime/size penalties in the hot inner loops that dominate this benchmark's execution time, so they should apply selectively rather than broadly; IGV is cheap and effective for hiding the program's small global state, so it stays enabled with balanced weights; SPLIT is enabled mainly as a diversity multiplier that improves the effectiveness of FLA and BCF, with slightly raised CorrectnessRisk weight reflecting care around basic-block splitting in optimized C++ code. All CorrectnessRisk weights are kept low-to-moderate to bias selection away from fragile transformations, preserving correctness while keeping aggregate runtime and size overhead acceptable.
